stories.head: The Pentagon now says it dropped Anthropic, the AI firm it labelled a security risk.
stories.body: Sources say Anthropic's Claude AI was still used for intelligence work last week. On 3 October we reported Anthropic warning investors that this label could hurt its business.

stories.head: ChatGPT maker OpenAI reportedly wants to raise $30 billion or more from investors.
stories.body: United Arab Emirates funds and investment firm BlackRock are in talks, valuing OpenAI at about $1.4 trillion. We first reported the plan on 30 September; the backers' names are new, and details could change.

stories.head: Chinese AI lab DeepSeek is reportedly close to raising at least $12 billion.
stories.body: Tencent, the company behind WeChat, and battery maker CATL are among the biggest backers. The sum beats DeepSeek's first target, but unnamed sources say details could still change.

stories.head: Chinese AI firm Moonshot reportedly plans a Hong Kong share sale early next year.
stories.body: Moonshot, which makes the Kimi AI models, is now valued at about $50 billion. The timing may still change, and Chinese regulators are reportedly investigating its data security.

stories.head: Wikipedia's parent says OpenAI's AI agents tried to edit pages without approval.
stories.body: The agents' millions of automated requests may have helped cause a partial outage in May. No sign of data theft was found, and OpenAI says it is studying the activity.

stories.head: Hackers who stole bank customer data may have used AI, South Korea's president says.
stories.body: Officials have not said which AI tools were used or how much data was taken. On 4 October we reported the president ordering an investigation; AI was then only suspected.

stories.head: AMD, Nvidia's closest rival, says it will supply far more AI chips in 2027.
stories.body: Boss Lisa Su says AMD needs more advanced chip-making capacity as demand stays very high. She spoke in Taiwan while visiting suppliers, but gave no figures.

stories.head: Google is reportedly near a deal for power from America's biggest nuclear operator.
stories.body: The operator, Constellation Energy, made a similar deal with Amazon last week. Tech firms want round-the-clock power for AI; Google would pay $1 billion or more.

stories.head: LG and Nvidia are reportedly building an AI brain to help drive future Hyundai cars.
stories.body: The AI would watch the road and predict what happens next, unnamed sources say. Hyundai plans cars with Nvidia's driving help from 2028 but has not announced LG's part.

stories.head: A new US-made AI, Beam, matches a top Chinese model on reasoning, its maker says.
stories.body: Start-up Reflection says Beam needs far less computing power; outsiders have not checked this yet. On 5 October we reported Reflection's plan to rival Chinese models anyone can run.

stories.head: Google DeepMind says its AI invented two enzymes, proteins that speed up chemistry.
stories.body: The first makes a drug ingredient 99 times faster than today's factory method, DeepMind says. The other breaks down a risky plastic softener; outside experts have not checked either.

stories.head: Former AI workers warned New York City's council that their old firms are reckless.
stories.body: Ex-Anthropic engineer Jacob Coxon said humanity will probably lose control of AI on the current path. Staff at AI companies said safety is their focus; the council is considering having outsiders approve AI systems.

stories.head: An app's AI now looks at faces and prescribes acne medicine for people in Utah.
stories.body: Start-up Nolla Health claims a US first: AI that starts new prescriptions, not just renewals. Doctors approve each prescription for the first 100 patients, then check less as patient numbers grow.

stories.head: Britain will check AI medical tools throughout their use, not just once.
stories.body: The government answered a September report from NHS doctors, accepting all its proposals. Such AI can change as doctors use it; the detailed rules are still unwritten.

stories.head: Protesters disrupted a London tech dinner as anti-AI groups report more sign-ups.
stories.body: The protesters belong to Pull The Plug, a group that favours direct action. The head of another group, PauseAI, calls such action extremely counterproductive.

stories.head: Some Alexa assistants got stuck saying "la, la, la," and Amazon says it's a bug.
stories.body: Users say the la-la-la sometimes lasted several minutes, and Amazon says a fix is coming. A couple of months ago, Alexa startled users with sounds like a snarling animal.

teaser.head: NATO's top general is drafting a plan using drones and AI to beat a Russian attack.
A US senator replied to the AI warnings of Anthropic's boss, calling them alarmist.
An AI steered a US lab's X-ray imaging machine from plain-English requests, the lab says.
Qualcomm went to trial against chip designer Arm, seeking to stop paying it royalties.

bp.head: Tech shares hit a record; banks and Gulf Arab funds line up money for AI.
bp.body: Gulf Arab funds may back OpenAI; banks are selling a $60 billion AI chip loan. Watch long-term US interest rates, highest since 2002: they raise AI loan costs.
